clue.text: Medic with American colleagues in crisis

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
the AMA, the American Medical Association, is the professional body of a doctor's US colleagues

explanation.surface: A doctor working alongside US counterparts during an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: The AMA is the American Medical Association, so 'American colleagues' are fellow doctors, picking up the medical theme of 'Medic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis full of tension and excitement is loosely called a drama, as in making a drama out of something.

clue.text: No chance of resolution in The Mystery of the Murdered Rugby Player?

parts.note: someone murdered is dead
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A detective novel's title, about a murdered rugby player, said to leave no hope of solving it.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue frames the pieces as a whodunit title. In rugby the lock is a forward in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standoff where neither side can move, so no settlement is possible.

clue.text: Misanthrope will block any element

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in the middle of it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Timon of Athens, in Shakespeare's play, is the classic misanthrope

explanation.surface: A people-hater who will obstruct anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is the man-hater of Shakespeare's play; his name goes inside ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a chemical element, a brittle metalloid with the symbol Sb.

clue.text: Bats heading off in a great crowd

indicators.note: the head of the word is taken off, so its first letter goes

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, as is barmy

explanation.surface: A swarm of bats flies off in a huge mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the flying animals but is the adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast throng of people is often called an army, as in an army of fans.

clue.text: Line in amusing taunt that can be swapped

parts.note: amusing means fun

indicators.note: the line letter is placed in the taunt word

parts.note: a gibe is a taunt

explanation.surface: A bit of comic mockery that could be traded for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungible goods are interchangeable, one unit replaceable by another of the same kind.

clue.text: One receives broadcast sequence, still not recognised

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it as a recipient takes delivery

parts.note: unified means made one
an ident is the short sequence a TV channel shows to identify itself

explanation.surface: A viewer receives a programme sequence but still can't place it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is an adjective here: made into one, UNIFIED. An ident is the brief branded clip between TV programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unidentified has not yet been named or placed, so it remains unknown.

clue.text: Leaving after Independent denied award

indicators.note: the Independent letter is refused a place, so it is removed

parts.note: going means leaving

explanation.surface: Someone departing from the Independent newspaper misses out on an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as an OBE.

clue.text: Resist alien vessel

parts.note: to buck a trend is to resist it
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Fighting off an extra-terrestrial spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket is a pail, a vessel for carrying liquid.

clue.text: Alter spaces in printing first of documents

parts.note: em and en are typographic spaces, the widths of letters M and N

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: An editor changes the spacing in the printing of the opening documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Em and en are the printer's units of space, named for the widths of the letters M and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or change it.

clue.text: Articles in English and French about corporation's fall

parts.note: A is an English indefinite article

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article
corporation is jocular old slang for a pot belly, as is tum

explanation.surface: Grammar notes on a company's collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is old humorous slang for a paunch, not a company; 'about' puts the French article around the belly word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American word for the season after summer.

clue.text: Boat covering length to attain point

indicators.note: the boat word wraps around the length letter

parts.note: a pinnace is a small ship's boat

explanation.surface: A vessel stretching its length to reach a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a peak, a pointed summit or spire.

clue.text: Very complimentary about girl and boy initially working in furnace conditions?

indicators.note: the praise word goes round the others

parts.note: a glowing report is full of praise
a lass is a girl

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the boy word is used

explanation.surface: Warm praise for a young couple who work in sweltering heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Glassblowers shape molten glass at a furnace, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Meat, first portion of which is swallowed by dog

indicators.note: the dog word eats up the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a lab is a labrador
'which' refers back to the meat, so its first letter is M

explanation.surface: A hound gulps down the first bit of its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' points back to 'Meat', so the first portion is its initial M.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is the flesh of a young sheep eaten as food.

clue.text: Unpleasant expression in radio broadcast of tragic role

indicators.note: a radio broadcast is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic hero

explanation.surface: An actor's sneering voice during a radio performance of a tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, lecherous look, a nasty facial expression.

clue.text: The Queen and Edward work in the garden

parts.note: the royal we is how a monarch refers to herself
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: The monarch and a prince doing some gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch speaks of herself as 'we', the royal plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed is to pull unwanted plants from beds, a basic gardening task.

clue.text: Military operatives upset over submarine captain

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: military men are soldiers
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a fury over a naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels.

clue.text: Change to accommodate a tense dialogue

indicators.note: the change word houses the others within it

parts.note: a conversion is a change
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Making room for a fraught exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is a spoken exchange between people, as is a dialogue.

clue.text: Greasy plate's protection not initially required

indicators.note: the first letter is not needed, so it is dropped

parts.note: a doily is a lace mat set under a plate or cake

explanation.surface: A greasy dinner plate didn't need its mat in the first place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oily is covered in or full of grease.

clue.text: Rent reduction producing expression of emotion

parts.note: a rent is a rip or tear
a drop is a reduction

explanation.surface: A cut in the rent brings a tenant to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' suggests money paid for housing, but it is a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling tear is a visible sign of sadness or joy.

clue.text: Group skilfully limiting upturn in chaos

indicators.note: the skill word sets limits on either side of the other piece

parts.note: ably means skilfully

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mess is chaos

explanation.surface: A team deftly holding back a surge in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn in' reverses MESS to SSEM, which ABLY then holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people, a group.

clue.text: Bustles found in disarray, provoking suspicion

indicators.note: disarray means disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Untidy bustles discovered, raising questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtfulness is a state of uncertainty or distrust, close to suspicion.

clue.text: Fate is fulfilled after end of luck

indicators.note: the rest comes after that letter
only the final letter of the luck word is used

parts.note: a demand that is met is fulfilled

explanation.surface: Destiny comes true once one's luck runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny, a word from Turkish via Arabic.

clue.text: Winter sports accessory, without question, getting you to glide over the surface

indicators.note: the question word is left out

parts.note: a ski mask protects the face on the slopes
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A piece of winter sports gear that unquestionably lets you glide across the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without question' reads as 'certainly' but asks for ASK to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim is to move lightly over a surface, barely touching it.

clue.text: Baby son going to shops

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A baby boy heading off to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' looks like a noun but is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby as an adjective means small, as in baby carrots.

clue.text: End of Axis, European

definitions.meaning: each end of an axis, such as the earth's, is one of its two extremities
a native of Poland is a European

explanation.surface: A wartime alliance ends with one of the continent's peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole is either terminus of an axis, and a Pole is someone from Poland.

clue.text: Right limits to timber usage

indicators.note: the limits are each word's outer letters

explanation.surface: Correct restrictions on how wood is used.
explanation.definitionFit: True means correct or accurate, as does right.

clue.text: Frontrunners of wild horses obeying a request to stop

indicators.note: the front runners are the leading letters of each following word

explanation.surface: The leading wild horses heed a call to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry used to make a horse halt, also said to slow anyone down.

clue.text: Liberal politician, Welsh, not quite in senior position

indicators.note: the word is not complete, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: high means in a senior position

explanation.surface: A Welsh Liberal who hasn't quite made it to the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were the British party that became the Liberals in the 19th century.

clue.text: Amateur to take charge of weapon at the front

indicators.note: the weapon word comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
to chair a meeting is to take charge of it

explanation.surface: A novice leading an armed unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic is a theorising non-expert with no practical experience.

clue.text: Youngster cuddling woman's sweet child

indicators.note: the young-animal word embraces the other piece

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
her means belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A little one cuddling a woman's darling baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic-looking, chubby infant, so any adorable child.

clue.text: Greatly hampered with husband's unwillingness to move

indicators.note: letters hampered are disrupted and thrown out of order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Badly held back by her husband's reluctance to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggishness, a lack of energy to act.

clue.text: Fish very quietly snared by man

indicators.note: the man word traps the other inside it

parts.note: a guy is a man
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: A fish silently caught by an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: The guppy is a small, brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish.
